picks.reasoning: Skill wins games, and T1 has the best players on this Rift. Faker, Keria and Peyz have been in this spotlight for years, and the reigning world champs don't fold against a CBLOL side that hasn't proven itself on this stage. LOS has the fun comeback story, but I won't back hype over individual class, and T1's lineup outclasses theirs.

Look, I live for the first 15 minutes, and LOS actually has the better early profile with their tower control, so they can absolutely scare T1 on tempo. But the big region gap is the loudest thing on this board, and reigning world champs T1 know how to stabilize and take over once the first dragon and herald fights get messy. Faker's squad cleans up the map when jungle pathing gets tight, and I trust that pressure at the Worlds stage over a CBLOL team that hasn't beaten LCK yet.

Under Fearless Draft, this is about who has the deeper well of champions and who stays calm when the bans start stacking. T1 have the reigning world champion's playbook and stars who've lived on this stage, and that should win the draft. LOS have real flair, with Ryze and Pantheon comps and a Kai'Sa that could pop off, but the LCK gap is too big for me to pick against T1 in a single game.

I don't lean hard often, but the region gap here is the clearest number on the board: CBLOL is 0-3 against the LCK this year and T1 are reigning world champions. LOS have the better recent form and some real comeback grit, but T1's last 20 games (9-11) tell me they aren't unbeatable, so I'm staying measured. In a single game, I'll still back the champs to figure it out.

LOS are riding a lovely wave right now, and that comeback energy tells me this group really believes in each other. But T1 are the reigning world champions, and a locker room that has lifted the trophy before carries a calm that's hard to fake on a Worlds stage. Keria's steadying presence and that veteran composure should hold when the nerves hit, though I wouldn't be shocked if LOS's belief makes it a scrappy one.
